chains.title: GATA2 binds the risk ref C allele more strongly at a distal LMO1 enhancer, increasing LMO1 expression and neuroblastoma risk

links.claim: The ref C allele binds GATA2 more strongly than the alt A allele. The literature strand calls this G/T, so ref C corresponds to the risk G allele and alt A to the protective T allele. GATA2 is selected because it is highly expressed in SK-N-SH (rank 17), has a SK-N-SH ChIP-seq peak over the variant, and has its own QBiC-SELEX model with a strong ref-biased change (z -56.07, effect -0.816). ChIP supports occupancy in the region, not allele-specific occupancy.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E1518342) with DNase, H3K27ac, H3K4me3 and TF ChIP-seq occupancy, consistent with a regulatory element.

LMO1 is the nearest plausible target gene, lies 34.9 kb away, and is the best L2G gene for this variant. The alt A allele is associated with lower LMO1 expression in GTEx skeletal muscle, but no adrenal-gland eQTL was reported, so this direction is tissue-limited.

SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells express high GATA2 and show GATA2 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant. Literature links the rs2168101 GATA/TATA motif to adrenergic neuroblastoma state, with the risk GATA allele corresponding to ref C.

If stronger GATA2 binding at the risk ref C allele raises LMO1 expression, this is predicted to promote the adrenergic neuroblastoma state and metastasis, while the protective alt A allele would lower LMO1. GATA2-specific causality is inferred from motif literature and is not directly proven.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP in a heterozygous neuroblastoma line shows higher GATA2 occupancy on ref C than alt A.
A C vs A enhancer reporter in SK-N-SH shows higher activity for ref C than alt A.
GATA2 knockdown or CRISPRi in SK-N-SH reduces LMO1 expression and enhancer activity.
The risk ref C allele is associated with higher LMO1 expression in an adrenal/neuroblastoma-relevant context.
falsified_if: Allele-specific reporter or ChIP assays show a reproducible C vs A difference at this base.
GATA2 perturbation changes LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH in the predicted direction.
Fine-mapping excludes linked causal variants and supports rs2168101 as the causal base.

chains.title: GATA3 may act through the same GATA motif, with ref C binding more strongly and increasing LMO1

links.claim: The ref C allele binds GATA3 more strongly than alt A. GATA3 is expressed and has SK-N-SH ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant. E35 shows GATA3 has its own QBiC-SELEX model with a ref-biased change (effect -4.206), though GATA2 has higher expression and overlapping motif specificity.
The variant is in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE with chromatin marks and TF occupancy.

LMO1 is nearby and is the strongest L2G gene. GTEx skeletal muscle shows alt A associated with lower LMO1, but adrenal-gland eQTL data were negative, so the expression direction is not confirmed in the most relevant tissue.
GATA3 is expressed in SK-N-SH and occupies the variant by ChIP-seq, supporting a possible role in this neuroblastoma cell context.

If GATA3 is the relevant GATA factor, stronger ref C binding would increase LMO1 and promote neuroblastoma, while alt A would reduce LMO1 and risk. This remains conditional because the literature supports a general GATA-motif effect rather than GATA3 specifically.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP shows higher GATA3 occupancy on ref C than alt A.
GATA3 knockdown reduces LMO1 expression or reporter activity in SK-N-SH.
The C/A enhancer effect is partly GATA3-dependent and not solely GATA2-dependent.
falsified_if: GATA3 depletion does not affect LMO1 expression or enhancer activity in SK-N-SH.
Allele-specific assays show the differential GATA occupancy is accounted for by GATA2 rather than GATA3.
The GATA3 QBiC-SELEX signal is shown not to reflect GATA3 binding at this motif.

chains.title: FOXJ3 binds the alt A allele more strongly and may repress LMO1, reducing neuroblastoma risk

links.claim: The alt A allele binds FOXJ3 more strongly than ref C. FOXJ3 is expressed and occupied at the variant in SK-N-SH, and QBiC-SELEX shows an alt-biased change, but the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped FOXG1 model, so the allele-specific binding evidence is weaker and not fully FOXJ3-specific.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE, so an allele-specific FOXJ3 site could modulate enhancer activity.

The element is near LMO1, the best L2G gene, and alt A is associated with lower LMO1 expression in GTEx skeletal muscle; adrenal eQTL data are negative, so this is not confirmed in the most relevant tissue.
FOXJ3 is expressed in SK-N-SH and has ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant.
If FOXJ3 represses LMO1, stronger alt A binding would lower LMO1 and reduce neuroblastoma risk. There is no direct evidence that FOXJ3 represses LMO1, so this phenotype link is speculative.

predictions: Alt A increases FOXJ3 occupancy at the enhancer.
FOXJ3 depletion increases LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH if FOXJ3 is a repressor.
The alt A reporter effect is reversed by FOXJ3 knockdown if FOXJ3 mediates repression.
falsified_if: FOXJ3 depletion decreases rather than increases LMO1 expression.
Allele-specific FOXJ3 ChIP or reporter assays show no alt A effect.
FOXJ3 is not shown to repress LMO1 or enhancer activity in neuroblastoma cells.

E18f/g support a GATA-motif allele effect on LMO1 expression and neuroblastoma phenotype, but they do not directly prove that GATA2 is the functional mediator or that GATA2-driven LMO1 increases risk.

To better understand this synergy, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on primary tumors from transgenic zebrafish overexpressing MYCN alone or with LMO1.

Our data suggest that LMO1 overexpression in MYCN-amplified NB cells increases the pro-metastatic properties of macrophages in the tumor-cell microenvironment, which is important for driving NB metastasis.
We found LMO1 rs2168101 G > T and rs11603024 C > T as well as LMO2 rs7933499 G > A were significantly associated with Wilms tumor risk.

Stratified analysis demonstrated a protective role of rs2168101 GT/TT genotypes against Wilms tumor in the subgroups of age ≤ 18 months, males and clinical stages I/II compared to the rs2168101 GG genotype.

Fourteen loci, including ten protective polymorphisms from CASC15, BARD1, LMO1, HSD17B12, and HACE1, and four risk variants from BARD1, RSRC1, CPZ and MMP20 were significantly associated with neuroblastoma risk.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.

Here, we showed that WT zebrafish with the GATA genotype developed adrenergic neuroblastoma, while knock-in of the protective TATA allele at this locus reduced the penetrance of MYCN-driven tumors, which were restricted to the mesenchymal cell state.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.

The authors previously showed that overexpression of LIM-domain-only 1 (LMO1), a transcriptional coregulator, synergizes with MYCN to accelerate tumor formation and metastasis in an NBL-zebrafish model.
